blocks.text: This page tracks the Port Coquitlam MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $840,200 for a typical home, down 6.9% over twelve months.
Port Coquitlam benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Port Coquitlam home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $840,200 in October 2026. That is little changed at +0.6% on the month, down 3.3% over three months, down 5.9% over six months and down 6.9% over the year. Over three years it is down 10.8%, and over five years little changed at −0.9%.
The weakest one-year move in Port Coquitlam was for a detached home homes at −8.4%; the strongest was a townhouse at −3.3%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,235,900) and an apartment ($551,200) is $684,700, and a townhouse ($854,900) sits $303,700 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, Port Coquitlam is 21.4% below. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against down 6.9% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Port Coquitlam ranks 17 by all-home benchmark, with Maple Ridge above it at $864,000 and Pitt Meadows below it at $832,600.

Detached homes in Port Coquitlam: benchmark $1,235,900, little changed at −0.4% in a month, down 5.6% in three months, down 6.8% in six months, down 8.4% in a year, down 10.4% in three years and down 2.5% in five. That is 30.4% below the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in Port Coquitlam: benchmark $854,900, up 2.5% in a month, little changed at +0.3% in three months, down 4.7% in six months, down 3.3% in a year, down 9.7% in three years and up 2.6% in five. That is 15.1% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in Port Coquitlam: benchmark $551,200, little changed at +0.2% in a month, down 3.4% in three months, down 5.0% in six months, down 7.6% in a year, down 11.5% in three years and up 2.4% in five. That is 18.1% below the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Port Coquitlam home is worth about $62,300 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $902,500. By type, detached homes lost about $113,300, from $1,349,200 to $1,235,900, townhouses lost about $29,200, from $884,100 to $854,900, and apartments lost about $45,300, from $596,500 to $551,200 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $892,900 six months ago and near $941,900 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $52,700 below the six-month mark and about $101,700 below the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the Port Coquitlam benchmark is about $228,400 below the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $224,700 below.
Port Coquitlam sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 192 Port Coquitlam houses sold at a median of $1.29M (middle half $1.16M to $1.41M), half of them within 22 days. 234 condos sold at a median of $560,000 (middle half $468,125 to $630,000), half within 25 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.33M to $1.22M between November–January and August–October (37 and 52 sales).

blocks.text: What the Port Coquitlam figure is
The $840,200 Port Coquitlam figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for October 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Port Coquitlam?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Port Coquitlam home was $840,200, with detached at $1,235,900.

faq.q: Are Port Coquitlam home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Port Coquitlam is down 6.9% over twelve months and down 3.3% over three months.
